images.title: The place value chart with the new TTh column
images.purpose: Show that the chart gets a new column, TTh, to the left of Th, and that 10,000 is a 1 in TTh with four zeros.
images.composition: One wide place value chart centred on white, five columns, with the number 10,000 written in it and a small arrow showing ten thousands joining into one ten thousand.
images.exact_structure: A table with a header row and one number row. Header cells left to right: TTh, Th, H, T, O, each in its own colour: TTh in #CC79A7, Th in #0072B2, H in #009E73, T in #E69F00, O in #6B7280. Number row digits left to right: 1, 0, 0, 0, 0. The TTh header cell has a thin #CC79A7 ring and a small tag above it reading 'new column'. Under the chart, a thin line joins the Th cell to the TTh cell with an arrow labelled '10 thousands = 1 ten thousand'. Below the arrow, the comma number 10,000 is written large. No other decoration.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Ten thousands make one ten thousand, which goes into a new column called TTh.
